talks.title: TROOPERS24: Keynote
talks.teaser: Demonstrates keynote - A question of time and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Industry Evolution and Tooling

Keynote speaker Guillaume Arcas of Google Mandiant Flare reflects on TROOPERS' history and warns newcomers against over-relying on current tools. Fundamentals matter when tooling fails—past tools like w32dasm disappeared, and even IDA faces uncertain futures.

AI Limitations

He tested feeding a modified malware decryption algorithm to AI, which returned a confident but wrong answer without doubt. AI adds a new factor to the attacker-defender game, but human expertise and skepticism remain essential.

Learning Through Failure

Arcas advocates embracing mistakes and uncertainty as normal learning steps, rejecting cultures that punish failure or idolize flawless experts. Education systems wrongly glorify top performers while dismissing those who repeat grades.

Individual Expertise

Everyone possesses unique knowledge others lack. His first conference talk came after realizing colleagues overestimated what others already knew—a lesson about connecting outside one's bubble to recognize personal value.

talks.title: The Red Teamer’s Guide to Deception
talks.teaser: Analyzes the Red Teamers Guide to Deception and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Why Red Teams Still Win

Balazár and colleagues from SBS red teaming show real engagement shells and walk through cases—telecom Linux lateral movement, financial password spraying to core banking, and manufacturing AD attacks—where detections fired but failed to evict attackers.

SOC Reality

They argue SOC teams struggle with incomplete log coverage, noisy legacy tools mimicking attacker behavior, alert fatigue, and analysts who lack domain context. Determined attackers retry until they slip through sparse medium-severity alerts.

Internal Honeypots as Smoke Detectors

The speakers advocate cheap internal deception: fake credentials, canary hosts, and tripwires that almost never false-positive because legitimate users never touch them. Alerts warrant senior analyst response and slow attackers who must question every vulnerability.

Vendor Case Study Caution

A deployed commercial deception product on all laptops failed when the team entered via a non-laptop vector and never triggered embedded tokens. Their lesson: simple, environment-tailored honeypots with admin buy-in beat over-engineered rollouts.

talks.title: Fuzzing at Mach Speed: Uncovering IPC Vulnerabilities on MacOS
talks.teaser: Reviews fuzzing at Mach Speed: Uncovering IPC Vulnerabilities on MacOS and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Speaker and audience

Mandiant/Google consultant Dylan Frankie presents year-long research on fuzzing macOS Mach IPC, aimed at offensive researchers and defensive engineers alike.

Fuzzing basics

Fuzzing sends unexpected inputs through attack vectors to trigger crashes in memory-unsafe C/C++ code, potentially exposing buffer overflows, use-after-free, and similar bugs.

Approach

He contrasts mutation-based fuzzing (mutating valid inputs) with grammar-based fuzzing, focusing on mutation for this work. The fuzzing cycle is his framework for finding and refining memory-corruption issues.

macOS IPC focus

The XNU Mach layer handles low-level IPC. Mach ports act as kernel-managed mailboxes; services register with the bootstrap server (e.g., com.apple.Troopers) so clients can allocate ports, register services, and exchange messages. He argues base Mach IPC is a high-value target because many higher-level mechanisms build on it.

talks.title: How to travel the C SAFely with .json when there are no Argonauts
talks.teaser: Details how to travel the C SAFely with .json when there are no Argonauts and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Overview
Dina from Germany's BSI maps coordinated vulnerability disclosure onto the myth of Jason and the Argonauts, using CSAF JSON advisories as the modern "fleece" that helps researchers and vendors navigate disclosure safely.

## The Disclosure Problem
Reporting a vulnerability feels like encountering an unknown "Minotaur": unclear policies, missing security.txt files, and fear of legal or professional retaliation. She contrasts manufacturer-centric "responsible" disclosure with coordinated disclosure mediated by neutral bodies.

## CSAF and BSI's Role
CSAF provides machine-readable JSON for security advisories, enabling automation across government and industry. BSI acts as Medea—holding the fleece, brokering public advisories at the end of CVD, and shielding researchers when vendors push back.

## Takeaways
Organizations should publish security.txt, adopt CSAF, and treat coordinated disclosure as a shared journey—not a back-room negotiation.
